analysis: Docs-only units examined. docs/developer/test.md head lines 480-1150 are unchanged surrounding text in this batch (changed head ranges are 3, 117-143, 197-224, in another batch); they describe test suites for checkpoint storage, endpoint resumption, logout, App Attest dispatch and Flint/Nemotron, with no new security claims here. docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes: date bump (line 3); GLM video input now documented as constant or variable frame rate (head 52), a parsing-surface statement for decrypted media (TB-007, T-050) whose implementation is not supplied; new state-file row (head 1578) documenting ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json (0600, DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE), managed GLM load hashes bound to file identities and reused for startup registration; memory_reserve_gb note (head 1604) now says OS availability may include reclaimable file page cache (availability/admission only). Material integration question: the VerifiedWeightHashStore caches weight hashes in an operator-writable home directory and reuses them for startup registration. Under TB-003/ADV-001, an operator can edit a 0600 file they own; per A-004/T-012/T-027, weight hashes are self-reported anyway, and the file-identity binding (inode/size/mtime?) may allow weight substitution preserving identity metadata unless the load path re-verifies. Also the hash feeds the T-041 SSD cache binding (verified weightHash in coordinator mode). Source VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift and GLM5Next load/registration paths were not supplied; test.md 117-143 claims a same-size corrupted shard leaves the digest unset and no load-time WeightHasher pass runs. Integration should verify that cached hashes cannot be reused after file content changes (e.g., mtime-preserving replacement) and whether the threat model (A-004, T-012, T-027, T-041) needs updating for this cached-hash trust assumption. No finding raised from docs alone.
